answer: A strong Sybil brake is a locked proof-of-cost bond posted per identity. Launching a fleet of fake accounts forces the attacker to fund every bond from real capital at once, and those funds sit idle earning nothing until the epoch closes, so a thousand identities mean a thousand times the yield forfeited. Each key also has to be anchored to a distinct hardware witness, like a unique shale sampling point, registered jetty terminal, or basalt quarry site, so one device cannot seed many accounts, and reputation decays, meaning a new identity starts at zero.
